# dsh-opencodego-usage
**OpenCode Go subscription usage in the DeepSeek Harness composer.** The 5-hour, weekly and monthly
windows live in a compact pill in the composer tool row, inside the shared centered pill group; clic
k it for a DSH-style details dialog with reset countdowns, colors and a manual refresh.
Zero configuration. The plugin uses the OpenCode Go provider key DSH already stores — no cookie, no
workspace ID, no settings page.
**Español** → README.es.md
**Project page** → jmolo.es/proyectos/dsh-opencodego-usage
*The details window: one percentage, one thin progress bar and one local reset countdown per window,
followed by last update, auto-refresh cadence, source and a manual refresh. The chat background is
blurred for privacy.*
*The compact pill: the OpenCode mark and three context-style rings separated by `·`. It joins the sh
ared centered pill group used by the other JaMoLpE88 plugins and is visible only with an OpenCode Go
model; with several pills visible they sit side by side, centered, with a small gap.*
## What it does

- Shows the three OpenCode Go windows in one compact pill: **5-hour**, **weekly** and **monthly**.
-
Uses the same context-style rings as DSH's own context meter, with `·` separators between windows.
- Colors the ring and bar by severity with the same mint, amber and coral palette as the DeepSeek ra
te clock: mint below 50 %, amber from 50 % to 74 %, coral from 75 % to 100 % (a rate-limited window

is always coral).
- Opens a native-looking details dialog on click: percentage, thin progress bar, r
eset countdown, local reset time, last update, auto-refresh cadence, data source and a **Refresh** b

utton.
- Counts down every second while the dialog is open. When a reset reaches zero, it performs a

n automatic fresh read so the window resets without user action.
- Refreshes the percentages every 6

0 seconds and when the app window becomes visible again.
- Appears only while the active model belon

gs to the `opencode-go` provider. Other providers show nothing.
- Appears in a new Session before th
e first prompt as well: while it records no model yet, the pill follows the model the composer displ

ays, including the configured default.
- Needs no settings: the provider key DSH already has is the

only credential.
- Joins the centered pill group shared with the other JaMoLpE88 composer plugins: w
ith several pills visible they sit side by side, centered, with a small gap, and hide together when
the row is too narrow.
## What it does not do

- It does not read OpenCode console cookies or scrape HTML.
- It does not ask for a key or store one

in the plugin.
- It does not keep usage history, telemetry or local storage.
- It does not add tool

s, commands or changes to the agent.
- It does not show anything when the active model is not from O

or changes to the agent.
- It does not show anything when the active model is not from OpenCode Go.
## Why there are no settings
If an OpenCode Go model is selected, the provider is configured and its key is already available to
DSH. The plugin resolves that key on the Host side and reads the official usage API. If no OpenCode
Go model is selected, the plugin has nothing useful to show and renders nothing.
There is no plugin config file, no key input, no threshold editor and no refresh preference. It is w
hat it is: the subscription data the provider already knows about.
## Requirements

- **DSH Desktop** `>= 0.2.1-rc.3`, profile `desktop` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`, Windows 11).
- An **Op

enCode Go** provider configured in **Settings → Models**, with a valid API key.
- Node 22+ (DSH ship

r configured in **Settings → Models**, with a valid API key.
- Node 22+ (DSH ships its own runtime).
If the provider is not configured you cannot select one of its models, so the plugin never appears.
That is intentional.
## How it works
The Host half calls the official OpenCode Go endpoint with the provider key:

It returns the three windows:

- The key is resolved from DSH's credential service (`OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`) on each read; `OPENCODE_

GO_API_KEY` in the process environment is the fallback.
- Results are cached for 55 seconds so the 6

0-second poll and multiple windows share one upstream request.
- Upstream failures keep the last kno

wn percentages and mark them **stale** instead of blanking the pill.
- The browser half reads two sa
me-origin routes: `/api/opencodego-usage` and `/api/opencodego-usage/refresh`. The key never reaches

the browser.
- Visibility uses the live `modelSelection` projection. Switching to another provider

hides the pill immediately; switching back shows it again.

## Compatibility

| DSH | `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (the only version tested by the author) |
| Node | `>= 22` |
| OS | Windows

11 (tested); macOS and Linux untested |
| Profile | `desktop` |
| Provider | OpenCode Go configured

in **Settings → Models** |
| Pill group | Shared with the other JaMoLpE88 composer pills (centered,

side by side) |
| Catalog | listed on dsh-plugin.org |
| Project page | jmolo.es/proyectos/dsh-openc

|

Validation status: **tested on Windows 11 with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-25). The pill appea
rs only with an OpenCode Go model, the details dialog opens, local reset times and countdowns update
, the severity colors follow the thresholds, and manual refresh works. The automatic refresh at a re
set is implemented with a one-shot guard; it is covered by the countdown path but was not observed d
uring a live reset in this validation.
Not validated: macOS, Linux, other DSH versions, and the web profile.
## Privacy

- No cookies, no browser session scraping, no workspace ID.
- The API key never leaves the Host proc

ess: the browser receives only percentages and reset timestamps.
- No configuration file, no local s

torage, no telemetry, no third-party requests beyond the official usage endpoint.
- The Host does no

t log the key or include it in error messages.
- The screenshots above were taken from a real sessio
n with the chat background blurred for privacy.
See SECURITY.md for the short policy.
